problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨3\sqrt{t},\,{csc}^{2}⁡(t)⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨4,\,10⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the components of the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t.$

$v(t)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$

feedback.problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨5,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4)+2⟩$ when $t=4,$ calculate the components of the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t.$

$v(t)=⟨$
{{field-1}},
{{field-2}}
$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,\text{d}t,\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{t}+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(4)=⟨5,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4)+2⟩.$ Substituting $t=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(4) & =⟨\sqrt{4}+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨5,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4)+2⟩ & =⟨2+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4)+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =2+{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{1} & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4)+2 & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(4)+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{2} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
v(t)=⟨\sqrt{t}+3,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+2⟩.
$$
